summary: feat(lyric): keep unplayed desktop lyrics white

decisions.title: Mark AMLL line play state in wrapper
decisions.rationale: Desktop lyrics need future lines to remain white while played and current lines keep the configured font color. The AMLL lyricBgLine class cannot distinguish past and future lines, while the wrapper can derive played/current/future from runtime line objects and current playback time without changing vendored AMLL code.
tradeoffs: Uses AMLL runtime internals through a narrow wrapper type.
Keeps the CSS override scoped to the desktop lyric window.
assumptions: AMLL DomLyricPlayer continues exposing currentLyricLineObjects with getLine and getElement.

rejected_alternatives.option: Override AMLL lyricBgLine colors directly
rejected_alternatives.reason: It cannot distinguish previously played lines from future lines and would affect the wrong text.

rejected_alternatives.option: Modify vendored AMLL line components
rejected_alternatives.reason: It expands the maintenance surface for a desktop lyric-only setting.

side_effects: Desktop lyric line elements receive data-lyric-play-state attributes while the feature is enabled.

summary: refactor(amll): integrate lyric core into source tree

decisions.title: Move AMLL runtime source into src/amll-core
decisions.rationale: The project now owns the AMLL runtime source as first-class source instead of carrying a nested vendor package with upstream demo, docs, and package metadata. This simplifies local imports, packaging, and CI validation for the desktop lyric player.
tradeoffs: Preserves AMLL runtime file contents during the move to reduce behavioral risk.
Drops upstream demo and test entry files that are not used by the app.
assumptions: Runtime resolution is controlled by webpack aliases rather than TypeScript path aliases for this integration step.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep vendor/applemusic-like-lyrics and alias into it
rejected_alternatives.reason: It leaves the code as an external vendor island and does not satisfy the integration goal.

rejected_alternatives.option: Fully normalize AMLL TypeScript style in the same change
rejected_alternatives.reason: That would mix a mechanical source-tree integration with a large semantic cleanup.

side_effects: CI now checks that src/amll-core exists and the old vendor directory is absent before platform builds.

decisions.title: Exclude imported AMLL core from project lint and typecheck initially
decisions.rationale: The imported upstream source uses patterns that do not match the current project compiler and lint rules, including extension-suffixed imports and Vite-oriented assumptions. Excluding it keeps the existing app checks green while preserving runtime bundling through webpack.
tradeoffs: AMLL core cleanup is deferred to a later focused pass.
Ambient declarations continue to provide app-facing types for AMLL imports.

bugs.symptom: ESLint reported six warnings after the migration-related cleanup.
bugs.root_cause: Removed diagnostic code left unused imports and helper paths, and the update download stream used non-null assertions plus an empty catch callback.
bugs.fix: Removed the unused memory telemetry hooks/imports and rewrote the download stream handling to avoid non-null assertions and empty callbacks.

decisions.title: Show a loading modal for subscription updates
decisions.rationale: Network plugin installation already shows a loading state through the input modal, but subscription update has no input step. A small reusable loading modal gives immediate feedback without forcing the no-input flow through an input component.
tradeoffs: Adds a generic modal template that may be reused by future async operations.
Keeps the subscription update button handler responsible for opening and closing the modal.

decisions.title: Read latest saved subscriptions before updating
decisions.rationale: The plugin manager page can hold a stale subscription array if the subscription modal saves data after the page rendered. Reading local storage again at click time keeps the manual update path aligned with the latest saved settings.
tradeoffs: Uses both the reactive hook value and a fresh storage read as fallback.
Trims and filters empty URLs before starting the batch.

bugs.symptom: Clicking update subscription appeared to do nothing while network install showed installing feedback.
bugs.root_cause: The subscription update path performed async installs without any visible loading state.
bugs.fix: Open a loading modal before the batch starts and close it before reporting success or failure.

bugs.symptom: Automatic plugin update IPC did not reach the main process reliably.
bugs.root_cause: The preload bridge used ipcRenderer.emit, which only emits locally, and the main listener passed an unbound instance method.
bugs.fix: Switched to ipcRenderer.invoke and ipcMain.handle with an arrow callback bound to the plugin manager instance.

summary: fix(ui): expand remaining music action hit areas

decisions.title: Apply full-container hit areas to remaining circular music actions
decisions.rationale: Commit dc9e60d fixed MusicFavorite inside MusicList card rows by letting the child component fill the circular action shell. The same mismatch still existed for download buttons and other circular action shells, so the fix needs to cover the reusable download component and all remaining call sites.
tradeoffs: Adds the same optional fillContainer contract to MusicDownloaded as MusicFavorite.
Keeps icon sizes unchanged while expanding only the actual clickable element.
Wraps playlist action icons in explicit circular option shells for consistent hit targets.

decisions.title: Keep the MusicBar comment action on the shell
decisions.rationale: The comment icon already has its click handler on the circular shell, so its hit area is already correct. The remaining issue was that disabled state only dimmed the button visually.
tradeoffs: Adds a click guard for unsupported comment plugins without changing the visual layout.

bugs.symptom: Some circular favorite/download actions only responded when clicking the icon center, not the full round button.
bugs.root_cause: The surrounding shell was styled as a circle, but the click handler lived on a smaller child component.
bugs.fix: Enabled fillContainer on MusicFavorite and MusicDownloaded in MusicList, MusicBar, and playlist action rows.

summary: fix(about): simplify attribution and add QQ group

decisions.title: Simplify About page attribution links
decisions.rationale: The About page should present the maintained BakaMusic repository, the reference desktop project, and the QQ group without separate original author or Android project rows.
tradeoffs: Keeps the link rows compact and removes redundant attribution rows.
Moves the visible row labels into existing language files for locale consistency.
assumptions: The reference project is MusicFreeDesktop by maotoumao and should remain linked directly.

decisions.title: Portal settings listbox panels
decisions.rationale: Settings listboxes were rendered inside setting rows, so later rows or sections could cover the dropdown through local stacking contexts. Rendering the options panel into the setting container with fixed positioning matches the already-fixed color picker behavior and applies to all ListBoxSettingItem usages.
tradeoffs: Keeps HeadlessUI Listbox semantics and virtual list rendering while moving the visual panel out of the row.
Repositions on scroll and resize instead of changing every individual setting row.

bugs.symptom: Languages, audio output device, and other settings dropdowns could be covered by later setting sections and become hard to adjust.
bugs.root_cause: Listbox options were absolutely positioned inside the row with a low local z-index, while following setting cards created competing stacking contexts.
bugs.fix: Render Listbox.Options through a portal into .setting-view--container and position it with getBoundingClientRect and fixed coordinates.

decisions.title: Expose Telegram group in About page
decisions.rationale: Users should be able to join the Telegram community from the same About page contact section as the QQ group. The visible label is Music Club while the link points to the Telegram invite URL.
tradeoffs: Adds localized labels for the row and display name in all existing language files.
Keeps the URL hardcoded with the other external project/community links in the About component.

decisions.title: Replace decorative header logo with a simpler mark
decisions.rationale: The previous BakaMusic header logo used a colorful italic wordmark with sparkle decoration. A single-color mark with a compact music glyph and clean wordmark better matches the app's refined header UI.
tradeoffs: Keeps the logo as the existing SVG asset so no component import changes are needed.
Uses currentColor to follow themed header text color instead of fixed gradient colors.

decisions.title: Add an explicit forced search path
decisions.rationale: The search hook intentionally skips duplicate first-page requests for the same query and plugin. A refresh button needs to bypass that guard and replace the current platform/type result with a new first-page request.
tradeoffs: Adds a narrow force option to the existing search hook rather than a separate refresh hook.
Keeps pagination behavior unchanged for normal load-more calls.

decisions.title: Expose refresh as a scoped search result action
decisions.rationale: Search failures can be retried without changing the selected media type or plugin. The button only calls search with the current query, current media type, and selected plugin hash.
tradeoffs: The first committed placement is beside the platform selector; a later UI pass can move it into the music list toolbar without changing the force-search API.

bugs.symptom: Repeating the same search on the same platform could not refetch results.
bugs.root_cause: The hook returned early when the requested query and page were already present for the plugin.
bugs.fix: Added a force option that clears current result data, marks the first page pending, and bypasses the duplicate-request guard.

decisions.title: Insert new songs at the top for custom-ordered local sheets
decisions.rationale: Custom sheet order is represented by sortType None and the persisted musicList array order. Appending new refs therefore always placed newly added songs at the end, which is inconvenient when users are manually curating the current top of a playlist.
tradeoffs: Changes only the insertion order for custom/manual local sheet order.
Keeps batch add order intact by prepending the selected batch as a group.
Leaves title/artist/album/newest/oldest sorted sheets on the previous append path because their display order is determined by the configured sorter.

bugs.symptom: New songs added to a manually custom-sorted playlist always appeared at the bottom.
bugs.root_cause: addMusicToSheet always appended new music references to the stored sheet musicList array, and custom order renders that array directly.
bugs.fix: When the sheet sort type normalizes to None, write new music refs before the existing stored list instead of after it.

decisions.title: Use a flat list row instead of stacked item cards
decisions.rationale: The previous redesigned row still read as one card per item. A single list surface with flat rows, separators, rounded hover states, and a subtle active stripe better matches dense music library browsing and avoids card stacking in local music views.
tradeoffs: Keeps the existing MusicList markup and virtual list implementation.
Moves cover sizing from inline style back into CSS so row sizing and visual treatment are controlled in one place.

decisions.title: Synchronize virtual row height with actual row box sizing
decisions.rationale: The visual overlap was caused by a fixed-height row containing a content-box card with padding, making the actual rendered item taller than the virtual list estimate. The card now uses border-box sizing and the estimate is aligned to the final row height.
tradeoffs: Uses a slightly taller flat row to give cover artwork and rounded hover backgrounds enough room.
Removes external row shadows to keep hover bounds aligned with separators.

bugs.symptom: Song list and local music rows visually overlapped, with each row's lower half colliding with the next row's upper half.
bugs.root_cause: The row card used height:100% with default content-box sizing, so its padding increased actual height beyond the virtual row height. The card-like shadow also made the mismatch more visible.
bugs.fix: Set the row card to border-box, align the virtual estimate to the actual row height, remove per-row card shadow, and use separator-based flat rows.

decisions.title: Remove the legacy MusicSheetlike card variant
decisions.rationale: Playlist, album, and recommendation sheet entries now share the cover-overlay treatment, so the older card variant was redundant and kept style branches alive across MusicSheetlikeItem and MusicSheetlikeList.
tradeoffs: Keeps the reusable MusicSheetlike components focused on the current overlay layout.
Requires affected callers to use the unified presentation instead of passing a legacy card mode.

decisions.title: Refresh README showcase assets with current UI states
decisions.rationale: The visual documentation should match the current player, home, playlist, settings, theme market, toplist, and dark mode screens after the sheet presentation cleanup.
tradeoffs: Updates documentation images in the same commit as the visible UI refactor to keep README screenshots aligned.

summary: fix(lyric): prevent desktop lyric border artifacts

decisions.title: Show desktop lyric windows only after first renderer paint
decisions.rationale: The transparent lyric BrowserWindow was created without show:false, so Electron could display the native transparent window before React and CSS finished the first paint. Deferring display until ready-to-show removes the startup edge flash while preserving a fallback timer for renderer failures.
tradeoffs: New lyric windows show themselves from the ready-to-show path instead of showLyricWindow showing them immediately.
A 2s fallback prevents a hidden window if ready-to-show does not fire.

decisions.title: Disable the native Windows thick frame for desktop lyrics
decisions.rationale: The remaining persistent black line was not a CSS edge; it matched the Windows DWM non-client border exposed by a frameless transparent BrowserWindow. The lyric window must remain resizable because desktop lyric sizing is a core feature, so the fix keeps resizable:true and disables only the thick frame/shadow/rounded-corner edge rendering.
tradeoffs: Native frame/shadow rendering is disabled for the lyric overlay while window resizing remains enabled.
Custom resize handles and Electron resize constraints stay available.

decisions.title: Force a Windows transparent-window recomposition after showing
decisions.rationale: Some Windows/Electron compositor paths can retain a stale transparent edge even after CSS has settled. A one-pixel width nudge after show forces DWM to recompose the transparent surface.
tradeoffs: Resize and move persistence are gated during the nudge so the workaround does not overwrite saved lyric window bounds.
The workaround is Windows-only and runs after show to avoid firing before the compositor has a visible surface.

decisions.title: Remove root-level rounded clipping from the lyric renderer document
decisions.rationale: Applying border-radius to html/body/#root can create anti-aliased transparent edge pixels that are cached by the transparent window compositor. The visible lyric page keeps its own rounded hover background without relying on root clipping.
tradeoffs: Root document no longer clips the entire transparent window shape; rounded visual treatment remains on the lyric page content.

bugs.symptom: Desktop lyrics briefly showed a container edge on startup, and for some users the edge stayed visible; after the first fix, a persistent black thin line still remained; disabling resizable then regressed the core window-size adjustment feature.
bugs.root_cause: The first fix handled renderer first-paint and CSS/compositor residue, but the persistent line came from the Windows native non-client thick frame/shadow on a frameless transparent BrowserWindow. The follow-up incorrectly disabled resizing along with the frame.
bugs.fix: Create the lyric window hidden, show it from ready-to-show after applying transparent background and lock state, remove root rounded clipping, keep resizable:true, disable thickFrame/hasShadow/roundedCorners edge rendering, and run a guarded Windows recomposition nudge after show.
bugs.lesson: Desktop lyric resize is core behavior; native frame artifacts must be removed without disabling BrowserWindow resizing.

summary: fix(lyric): dim inactive line-timed desktop lyrics

decisions.title: Mark desktop lyric line state independently from the unplayed-color setting
decisions.rationale: Line-timed desktop lyrics need current-line contrast regardless of whether users enable the separate setting that keeps unplayed lyrics white. The desktop lyric page now always requests row play-state attributes, while the main renderer remains on the shared component default.
tradeoffs: Desktop lyrics do a small per-frame state sync for visible AMLL lines.
The existing main-player lyric component is unaffected because it does not pass markLinePlayState.

decisions.title: Carry explicit line-vs-word timing metadata through AMLL lines
decisions.rationale: A line can contain one word and still be word-timed, so word count is not a reliable way to decide whether inactive-line dimming should apply. Mapping source lyrics to AMLL lines now records whether the original source had a word timeline, and the DOM wrapper forwards that metadata to data-lyric-timing.
tradeoffs: Adds a BakaMusic-specific metadata field to mapped AMLL lines.
The metadata is a plain structured-clone-safe property so AMLL's cloning step preserves it.

decisions.title: Use separate brightness behavior for line-timed and word-timed lyrics
decisions.rationale: The lyric brightness setting feels different between word-timed and line-timed lyrics. Word-timed lyrics should continue using the configured inactive brightness, while line-timed non-current rows use a fixed 70% opacity for stable row contrast.
tradeoffs: Line-timed inactive rows no longer follow lyric.inactiveBrightness.
Uses desktop lyric CSS attribute selectors scoped to line-timed rows.

bugs.symptom: Line-timed desktop lyrics kept every visible lyric line bright, so the current line lacked visual distinction.
bugs.root_cause: Play-state marking was tied to the unplayed-color setting, and the existing style only changed future-line color. Played line-timed rows remained fully bright like the current row.
bugs.fix: Always mark desktop lyric row state, propagate line-vs-word timing metadata, dim played/future line-timed rows to fixed 70% opacity, and keep word-timed lyrics on the configured inactive brightness.
bugs.lesson: Line-timed and word-timed AMLL lyrics need separate visual rules; settings that control word-timed brightness should not gate row-state data or line-timed contrast.

decisions.title: Persist the music detail cover style as renderer-local preference
decisions.rationale: The cover style is a main-renderer UI preference only, so it uses the existing user preference EventEmitter path instead of extending AppConfig or IPC contracts.
tradeoffs: The preference is local to the renderer and does not appear in settings.
The lyric toolbar selector and MusicDetail surface stay synchronized through useUserPreference.

decisions.title: Reuse the lyric toolbar menu placeholder for the cover style selector
decisions.rationale: The requested placement was the button to the right of lyric search. That button previously opened the lyric menu, while the same lyric menu remains available from the lyric panel context menu.
tradeoffs: Lyric font/download/link actions are now discoverable through right-click rather than a visible toolbar button.
The selector opens as a compact edge-aligned glass popover near the triggering button.

decisions.title: Use golden-ratio vinyl proportions for the album-art label
decisions.rationale: The UI treats album artwork as the center label, so a 61.8% label diameter gives the artwork enough visual weight while preserving record grooves around it. The 4.6% center hole remains visible without dominating the cover.
tradeoffs: This favors UI balance over a physically realistic small LP label.
Exact visual preference should still be checked in the Electron window.

summary: feat(music-detail): add selectable vinyl tonearm styles

decisions.title: Offer none/classic/glass tonearm variants as renderer-local preferences
decisions.rationale: The previous build hardcoded a single tonearm SVG. Exposing none/classic/glass through musicDetailVinylTonearm reuses the existing useUserPreference path consistent with musicDetailCoverStyle, keeping the choice local to the main renderer without touching AppConfig or IPC.
tradeoffs: The preference is not surfaced in the global settings page.
Selectors in the lyric toolbar popover and the MusicDetail surface stay in sync via useUserPreference.

decisions.title: Add an outer/inner drop-point option for the tonearm reach
decisions.rationale: A single fixed needle position cannot represent both the start (outer groove) and a deeper play position. musicDetailVinylTonearmReach lets the arm point to the outer or inner groove, and the reach selector is only shown when a tonearm is active.
tradeoffs: Adds a second conditional preference row that only appears for vinyl + non-none tonearm.
Exact arm geometry per reach is tuned in SCSS/SVG and should be smoke-tested.

decisions.title: Extract tonearm rendering into dedicated components
decisions.rationale: Replaced the inline SVG block in MusicDetail with GlassVinylTonearm and ClassicVinylTonearm components selected by preference, isolating each visual style and its reach-driven geometry.
tradeoffs: Two parallel SVG implementations must be maintained.
Shared ITonearmProps keeps the reach contract consistent across variants.

decisions.title: Fix descender clipping at the lyric word-wrapper level
decisions.rationale: Playback-page lyric descenders were clipped because the inline-block word wrappers inherited the player's tight global line-height. Setting line-height: normal on the main lyric wrappers restores font-metric-driven height without changing the global player rhythm or mask animation behavior.
tradeoffs: Targets the DOM lyric main-line wrappers only, so translation and roman lines keep their existing line-height.
Leaves the unrelated working-tree newline noise out of the staged commit.

bugs.symptom: Letters with descenders such as y, g, p, and q were visibly clipped at the bottom in the playback-page main lyric.
bugs.root_cause: The main lyric word wrapper spans are inline-block elements inheriting the AMLL player's tight line-height, producing a word box shorter than the font's descender metrics.
bugs.fix: Apply line-height: normal only to the main lyric wrapper spans so descenders fit inside the wrapper box while keeping the rest of the AMLL layout unchanged.
bugs.lesson: When glyph clipping follows the text box rather than the viewport, inspect inherited line-height on inline-block wrappers before changing masks or overflow.

summary: fix(amll): keep interlude dots tracking layout while paused

decisions.title: Fix inside InterludeDots.update() rather than the lyric scroll logic
decisions.rationale: The dots not following the scroll while paused was caused by update() returning early when not playing, which skipped the setTransform that applies calcLayout's recalculated position. Splitting the early-return so only time accumulation is guarded keeps the transform application path alive without touching the shared lyric scroll/layout code.
tradeoffs: Scoped to the interlude dots component only; no change to LyricPlayer scroll or calcLayout behavior.
update() now always rebuilds the style string even when paused, a negligible per-frame cost during interlude waits.

bugs.symptom: On a spacer/breathing line (the three-dot interlude wait), pausing playback froze the dots at fixed screen coordinates so they no longer scrolled with the lyrics.
bugs.root_cause: InterludeDots.update() returned early when this.playing was false, so the transform recomputed by calcLayout() was never flushed to the element style.
bugs.fix: Guard only the currentTime accumulation behind the playing check; always continue to build and apply the transform so the dots track the layout while paused.
bugs.lesson: When a paused element stops following layout updates, check for early returns that short-circuit the style/transform application, not just the time/animation state.

summary: feat(music-detail): default vinyl tonearm to none

decisions.title: Flip the tonearm fallback so the default is no tonearm
decisions.rationale: The vinyl tonearm fallback previously rendered the glass arm whenever the stored preference was unset or invalid. Inverting the guard to accept only glass/classic and otherwise fall back to none makes 'no tonearm' the default while preserving any explicit user choice.
tradeoffs: Mirrored in both the render path (MusicDetail/index.tsx) and the cover-style selector (widgets/Lyric/index.tsx) so the highlighted option stays in sync.
Existing users who picked glass or classic keep their setting; only unset/none/invalid values resolve to none.

summary: fix(amll): enlarge translation lines and highlight current line

decisions.title: Enlarge translation/roman sub-lines to the golden ratio
decisions.rationale: The sub-line font-size was 0.5em (50% of the main lyric), too small to read comfortably. Raised to 0.618em (golden ratio) for clear readability while keeping the main line dominant, matching the project's existing golden-ratio vinyl proportions.
tradeoffs: Only the active dom renderer's lyric-player.module.css changed; the unused dom-slim renderer and the desktop-lyric window (already 0.8em) were left untouched.

decisions.title: Highlight the current line's translation via renderMode rather than word-progress tracking
decisions.rationale: Keying off the existing GRADIENT renderMode (active line) to lift sub-line opacity avoids any new time/animation state and reuses the existing 0.2s opacity transition for a smooth fade. Chose 'always bright while current' over a 'flash on line-complete' pulse for better readability and far less complexity.
tradeoffs: Active line translation opacity 0.618 stays below the main lyric (1.0) to preserve hierarchy; inactive lines keep 0.3.
0.618 chosen to stay consistent with the golden-ratio font-size change.

bugs.symptom: In word-by-word (dynamic) lyrics the current line's translation/roman sub-line never brightened, staying dim from start to finish even while the main line was actively highlighted.
bugs.root_cause: dom/lyric-line.ts computed subopacity with a fixed 0.3 factor for all dynamic-mode lines, so the active line's translation got the same dim 0.3 as inactive lines.
bugs.fix: Detect the active line via renderMode === GRADIENT and use 0.618 opacity for its sub-lines, keeping 0.3 for the rest.
bugs.lesson: When an element never reacts to active state, look for a state-independent constant in its style computation, not the active-detection path.

summary: feat(native): add luna CENC proxy and private native CI

decisions.title: Keep native sources in a private repository
decisions.rationale: Native sources must stay out of the public BakaMusic repository while CI still needs platform-specific source builds. The private Zencok/baka-native repository is checked out into ignored native/ during CI and locally.
tradeoffs: Release builds now depend on the private repository and the NATIVE_REPO_DEPLOY_KEY secret.
CI fails intentionally if required native modules or outputs are missing instead of packaging stale binaries.

decisions.title: Use a read-only deploy key for private native checkout
decisions.rationale: A read-only deploy key limits CI access to Zencok/baka-native and avoids using a broad PAT for source checkout.
tradeoffs: The deploy key must remain enabled on baka-native and mirrored as a BakaMusic Actions secret.

decisions.title: Wrap Forge ignore instead of replacing it
decisions.rationale: Direct packagerConfig.ignore replacement broke the webpack and externals plugin chain. A local Forge plugin wraps the generated ignore function and adds only /native exclusion.
tradeoffs: The current behavior depends on Forge plugin resolve order, verified by npm run package.

decisions.title: Route CENC cek media through luna-proxy
decisions.rationale: Plugins can expose a 32-hex CENC content key, and the main-process plugin method registers the original media URL with luna-proxy to serve a local decrypted m4a stream with Range support.
tradeoffs: Playback depends on the luna-proxy service and ence.node being present; failures fall back to the original media source.

bugs.symptom: npm run package failed with existingIgnoreFn is not a function after setting packagerConfig.ignore as an array.
bugs.root_cause: @timfish/forge-externals-plugin assumes the webpack plugin has already installed a function-valued ignore handler.
bugs.fix: Replace direct ignore config with an inline Forge plugin instance that wraps the existing ignore function and excludes /native.
bugs.lesson: When using Forge webpack plus externals plugins, preserve plugin-generated packager config rather than replacing it directly.

bugs.symptom: Concurrent luna-proxy registrations could receive the wrong IPC response.
bugs.root_cause: The parent listener accepted any registered/error response from the child process.
bugs.fix: Add a requestId to register messages and filter child responses by that requestId.
bugs.lesson: Child-process request/response IPC needs correlation IDs once more than one request can be in flight.

summary: refactor(lyric): remove client-side Kuwo decryption, plugin handles it now

decisions.title: Remove client-side Kuwo lyric decryption entirely
decisions.rationale: The Kuwo plugin (kw.js) now implements full lyric decryption at plugin level, including lyricx word-by-word format with XOR yeelion key and buildKuwoWordLyric. Client-side isKuwoEncrypted/decryptKuwoLyric/autoDecryptLyric Kuwo branch were redundant and could cause incorrect decryption.
tradeoffs: QRC decryption remains in the client as no QQ Music plugin implements it.

decisions.title: Keep a vendored AMLL core baseline
decisions.rationale: BakaMusic depends on renderer behavior and appearance hooks that the published package API does not expose, so src/amll-core is rebased to the official 0.5.2 source rather than replaced by the npm runtime.
tradeoffs: Future upstream updates must reapply the documented BakaMusic patches.

decisions.title: Reapply local lyric presentation behavior
decisions.rationale: The 0.5.2 group and timeline architecture retains restrained blur, centered interlude support, inactive brightness, romanization ordering, sub-line emphasis, and descender fixes expected by the product.
tradeoffs: Local behavior is tracked in src/amll-core/UPSTREAM.md.

decisions.title: Reset the playback clock before resume
decisions.rationale: Re-anchoring RAF time to the latest media position prevents a long pause from being extrapolated into a transient next-line jump.

bugs.symptom: Inactive lyrics became heavily blurred after the 0.5.2 rebase.
bugs.root_cause: The upstream blur curve started at every inactive row.
bugs.fix: Restore the prior distance threshold and restrained falloff.

bugs.symptom: Line-level and word-level romanization appeared on different sides of the source lyric.
bugs.root_cause: The upstream DOM order placed fallback romanization below the main line.
bugs.fix: Restore word prepend and line child ordering so both modes render above.

bugs.symptom: Resuming after a long pause briefly selected the next lyric line.
bugs.root_cause: The RAF anchor timestamp still preceded the paused wall-clock interval.
bugs.fix: Synchronize media time and reset the RAF anchor before resuming animations.

summary: feat(ui): default music detail to vinyl cover

decisions.title: Use vinyl as the unset preference fallback
decisions.rationale: Fresh installs and users without a saved musicDetailCoverStyle now see the record presentation by default, while an explicitly saved cover preference remains respected.
tradeoffs: Users who never saved a preference will observe the new default but can switch back from the existing selector.

decisions.title: Use a 68px mini-mode cover
decisions.rationale: The 104px-tall mini window made the previous 56px artwork feel undersized, while the initial 72px adjustment was visually dominant. A 68px cover balances the available height and lyric width.
tradeoffs: The lyric column loses 13px of horizontal space compared with the prior layout, with existing ellipsis behavior handling overflow.

bugs.symptom: Album artwork looked too small after mini mode was made taller.
bugs.root_cause: The cover remained 56px inside a 104px-high window.
bugs.fix: Increase the cover and grid column to 68px, with matching gap and corner-radius adjustments.

decisions.title: Unify recent history and play counts

decisions.title: Combine notification state with foreground window geometry
decisions.rationale: Standalone borderless video players may cover a display without entering a Windows notification state that the existing detector recognizes, so poll the foreground window bounds as a fallback.
tradeoffs: The synchronous foreground-window query adds roughly a few milliseconds to the existing one-second Windows poll.
assumptions: A fullscreen player owns the foreground top-level window while its video is visible.

rejected_alternatives.option: Maintain a process-name whitelist

decisions.title: Match both outer and client bounds in raw and DIP coordinates
decisions.rationale: Requiring both rectangles to match a display within a small tolerance distinguishes borderless fullscreen windows from taskbar-constrained maximized windows, while Electron DIP conversion supports mixed-scale displays.
tradeoffs: Unusual player chrome or larger invisible borders may require a future tolerance adjustment.
assumptions: Fullscreen client content covers the selected display.
side_effects: Secondary monitors with negative coordinates are supported.

decisions.title: Ship get-windows as a CommonJS runtime external
decisions.rationale: Webpack cannot safely bundle node-pre-gyp's dynamic native binding lookup, and the legacy Forge externals plugin cannot inspect get-windows because its package.json is not exported. A small Forge plugin includes the external package and its JavaScript runtime dependency closure.
tradeoffs: The dependency and lockfile are larger, and packaging must retain the runtime dependency collector.
assumptions: The Electron 43 baseline with embedded Node.js 24 can synchronously require the ESM package.

rejected_alternatives.option: Bundle get-windows and node-pre-gyp
rejected_alternatives.reason: Optional development imports fail Webpack resolution and the dynamically located .node binary is not emitted.

side_effects: Windows x64 packaging now rebuilds and includes one additional native dependency.

bugs.lesson: Windows notification suitability is not a complete fullscreen signal; combine it with foreground-window geometry for generic player coverage.

decisions.title: Repair collapsed lines with invalid duration

rejected_alternatives.option: Apply a fixed duration to every line

bugs.symptom: Several local FLAC lyrics lost original rows, Japanese originals appeared under translation, and a WAV first lyric was attached to its preceding PV credit.

bugs.lesson: Embedded SYLT is often structurally valid but not canonical ESLRC, so preservation checks must precede semantic folding.

bugs.symptom: Same-timestamp local lyrics became inactive in under one second.
bugs.root_cause: Parallel folding retained a zero-duration main line, which the AMLL mapping only raised to its minimal display duration.
bugs.fix: Fill missing, non-finite, and non-positive line endings from the next distinct timestamp.

summary: feat(lyrics): write linked lyrics into local files

decisions.title: Materialize linked lyrics as rich embedded TTML
decisions.rationale: A local track linked through lyric search should be able to retain the currently parsed word timing, translation, romanization, ruby, duet, and background-vocal data inside the audio file.
tradeoffs: The embedded lyric is normalized to TTML rather than preserving the remote provider container byte-for-byte.
assumptions: The current LyricParser output is the canonical lyric currently shown to the user.

rejected_alternatives.option: Write only plain LRC
rejected_alternatives.reason: That would discard rich timing and vocal-layout information.

side_effects: A successful write clears the remote association so playback immediately reads the newly embedded lyric.

decisions.title: Perform tag mutation behind the NodeRuntime boundary
decisions.rationale: Renderer code should not access local files or Node tag APIs directly, and an existing user media file needs rollback protection.
tradeoffs: A same-directory temporary backup briefly duplicates the audio file.
assumptions: Local-library and explicitly granted paths remain covered by IPC path authorization.

rejected_alternatives.option: Write metadata in the renderer
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would violate the Electron process boundary.

side_effects: The writer verifies the persisted lyric and restores the backup after write failure.

decisions.title: Remove stale synchronized lyric frames and prefer complete TTML
decisions.rationale: ID3 USLT writes do not replace old SYLT frames, and music-metadata can otherwise return the old word entries before the new TTML document.
tradeoffs: Overwrite intentionally removes all prior ID3 synchronized and unsynchronized lyric frames.
assumptions: A complete embedded TTML document should take precedence over leftover per-word SYLT entries.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep every lyric frame and rely on order
rejected_alternatives.reason: Frame order varies and reproduced one word per displayed line.

side_effects: Previously affected files are recovered by TTML candidate priority and empty-namespace repair.

bugs.symptom: After overwriting an MP3 lyric, playback rendered hundreds of one-word lines that rapidly filled the lyric view.
bugs.root_cause: The old ID3 SYLT frame remained beside the new TTML USLT frame and received higher local-parser priority; browser XMLSerializer also emitted empty namespace resets in generated TTML.
bugs.fix: Remove SYLT and USLT before writing, prioritize complete TTML over synchronized word entries, strip empty namespace resets during generation, and repair existing TTML during parsing.
bugs.lesson: Replacing a generic lyrics property is not equivalent to clearing all format-specific lyric containers.

summary: fix(main): survive main-window destruction and bad plugin results

decisions.title: Latch a quitting flag on before-quit
decisions.rationale: A prevented window close cancels app.quit() after before-quit has irreversibly torn down subsystems, so the close handler must skip preventDefault once quitting.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep the tray removeAllListeners workaround
rejected_alternatives.reason: It strips every main-window listener and only masked the real quit-cancellation bug.

decisions.title: Re-create extension ports and guard destroyed windows everywhere
decisions.rationale: The port peer lives in the old renderer after main-window recreation, and destroyed BrowserWindow access throws inside tray/deep-link/ipc-security paths.

rejected_alternatives.option: Rely on window-all-closed to quit
rejected_alternatives.reason: It does not fire while a lyric/minimode window keeps the app alive.

decisions.title: Make the shared plugin host tolerate one bad plugin
decisions.rationale: A non-cloneable postMessage or an unhandled rejection would exit a host shared by all plugins, and an aborted restore loop leaves later plugins unloaded.

rejected_alternatives.option: Only sanitize the load path
rejected_alternatives.reason: The invoke reply path had the same structured-clone exposure.

bugs.symptom: Install-update on default Windows config left a hidden zombie process while the installer ran against locked files.
bugs.root_cause: The win32 minimize close handler preventDefault()'d unconditionally, cancelling app.quit() after teardown.
bugs.fix: Skip preventDefault once a before-quit quitting flag is set.
bugs.lesson: A prevented window close aborts an in-flight app.quit().

bugs.symptom: Tray commands crashed and all lyric/minimode IPC was denied after the main window closed with the app alive.
bugs.root_cause: The main-window reference was never nulled and destroyed-window access threw in message-bus and ipc-security.
bugs.fix: Null on 'closed', guard with isDestroyed(), and rebuild extension ports on recreation.
bugs.lesson: Optional chaining does not guard a destroyed Electron object.

summary: fix(download): scope worker recovery and lift watcher-scan timeout

decisions.title: Recover the worker only on runtime transport failures
decisions.rationale: Per-track errors must report ERROR in place; treating them as worker death restarts healthy downloads and loops the failing task forever.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep recovering on any thrown error
rejected_alternatives.reason: It conflates a single unavailable track with a dead runtime.

decisions.title: Give watcher-scan its own long timeout
decisions.rationale: The full-tree walk plus per-file metadata parse routinely exceeds 60s on large libraries, and the timeout kills the runtime shared with downloads.

rejected_alternatives.option: Chunk the scan
rejected_alternatives.reason: A larger dedicated timeout fixes the abort without reworking the scan protocol.

bugs.symptom: Batch-downloading an album with one unavailable track thrashed all downloads and retried the bad track endlessly.
bugs.root_cause: recoverDownloaderWorker ran for any error and bumped the failing task's runId before its ERROR check.
bugs.fix: Gate recovery on runtime transport failures and cap auto re-queues.
bugs.lesson: Shared-worker recovery must be reserved for actual transport death.

summary: fix(playback): recover failed loads and stabilize queue identity

decisions.title: Reload on same-media when the controller has no source
decisions.rationale: After a failed load seekTo/play are no-ops, so replaying the same track must take the full load path to retry.

rejected_alternatives.option: Always reload on same-media
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would discard the cheap replay path for the common already-loaded case.

decisions.title: Stop orphaned audio from the main process
decisions.rationale: A recreated renderer has an empty sourceId and the protocol has no sourceless stop, so only the main process can end the old libmpv source.

rejected_alternatives.option: Rely on the renderer to stop on teardown
rejected_alternatives.reason: The teardown is exactly when the renderer loses the sourceId.

decisions.title: String-key media identity and sparse sheet positions
decisions.rationale: Numeric vs string ids diverged from isSameMedia; dense position renumbering rewrote the whole relation table per edit.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep dense positions
rejected_alternatives.reason: Ordering only needs relative positions, so gaps are harmless and far cheaper.

bugs.symptom: Clicking a track that failed while offline did nothing after the network returned.
bugs.root_cause: The same-media fast path ran seekTo/play on a controller with no assigned source.
bugs.fix: Fall through to full load when hasSource is false.
bugs.lesson: A cheap replay path must verify the source is actually loaded.

summary: fix(lyrics): apply LRC offset to timeline and fix TTML romanization

decisions.title: Bake offset into the timeline once at parse time
decisions.rationale: Subtracting offset only in getPosition left progress and word search on unadjusted time; shifting all times once keeps every consumer consistent.

rejected_alternatives.option: Subtract offset in each consumer
rejected_alternatives.reason: AMLL views take raw item times and would each need to re-implement the shift.

decisions.title: Pair romanization by pre-filter line index
decisions.rationale: convertAmlLyricLines drops empty-text lines while the TTML base list is unfiltered, so array-position pairing misaligns after any gap.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep index-based pairing
rejected_alternatives.reason: It is only correct until the first dropped empty line.

bugs.symptom: Nonzero [offset:] desynced word highlight and line progress across all lyric views; empty TTML lines misaligned romanization.
bugs.root_cause: Offset was applied only to line selection, and romanization was assigned by post-filter position.
bugs.fix: Shift item/word/romanization times during parse and clear meta.offset; pair romanization by item.index.
bugs.lesson: Normalize timing offsets at the single parse boundary, not per consumer.

decisions.title: Word-bound feat/ft and space-flanked interpunct only
decisions.rationale: The old pattern matched ft mid-word and split CJK transliterated names, mangling single artists that a single-entry singerList expands unconditionally.

rejected_alternatives.option: Drop interpunct entirely
rejected_alternatives.reason: Some platforms do join artists with a spaced interpunct, which should still split.

bugs.symptom: 'Daft Punk' became 'Da'+'Punk' and '迈克尔·杰克逊' split into two artists.
bugs.root_cause: The split regex matched 'ft' without word boundaries and treated any interpunct as a separator.
bugs.fix: Require whitespace/word boundaries around feat/ft and spaces around the interpunct.
bugs.lesson: Separator heuristics need boundaries so they do not fire inside single names.

summary: perf(renderer): cut redundant list, lyric, and search work

decisions.title: Repair the MusicList memo comparator and stabilize call-site props
decisions.rationale: The sheet clause at the tail of the && chain returned false whenever musicSheet was absent, defeating memo for most views; inline literals also broke it.

rejected_alternatives.option: Drop the memo
rejected_alternatives.reason: The virtualized list with per-row quality lookups is exactly where memo pays off.

decisions.title: Gate hidden lyric subscriptions and cache search normalization
decisions.rationale: The panel stays mounted after close, and search fields are byte-identical between keystrokes, so both re-ran heavy work needlessly.

rejected_alternatives.option: Unmount the panel on close
rejected_alternatives.reason: keepMounted is required for the AMLL enter/exit motion.

bugs.symptom: Closed detail page reconciled the lyric subtree ~5-10x/sec; keystrokes re-normalized the whole local library.
bugs.root_cause: The panel subscribed to per-tick stores while hidden and the matcher normalized every field per invocation.
bugs.fix: Select constants when inactive and cache normalized/compacted values by raw string.
bugs.lesson: A retained-but-hidden subtree must not subscribe to per-tick stores.

summary: fix(app-config): bound legacy watch-dir migration grants

decisions.title: Bound the migration grant scope instead of requiring prior authorization
decisions.rationale: Legacy watch dirs never went through the dialog/drop grant flow, so assertPathAccess would break legitimate migration; rejecting roots, home and its ancestors, and system dirs bounds the blast radius instead.

rejected_alternatives.option: Call assertPathAccess per directory
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would reject valid user directories outside the builtin roots and defeat the migration.

decisions.title: Move filesystem probing off the main thread
decisions.rationale: Sync statSync/realpathSync on up to 128 renderer-supplied paths can stall the UI on a dead UNC path.

bugs.symptom: A compromised renderer could obtain a persistent recursive grant over an entire drive.
bugs.root_cause: The migration handler granted recursive access after only an existence check, unlike the normal watchDir write path.
bugs.fix: Reject overbroad roots and probe paths asynchronously before granting.
bugs.lesson: Every path-granting IPC entry needs the same authorization bounds.

summary: fix(app-config): persist plugin user variables and harden pluginMeta

decisions.title: Keep object-typed values in every config patch
decisions.rationale: Reference equality cannot prove a mutable object unchanged, so a caller that mutates the object returned by getConfig and passes the same reference back was silently dropped. The patch now always carries object values and lets the receiver decide against its own copy.

rejected_alternatives.option: Deep-equal comparison on object values
rejected_alternatives.reason: The in-place mutation already landed in the stored config before diffing, so a content comparison would still see no change and drop the write.

decisions.title: Fix the mutate-then-write shape at every call site, not only in the patch rule
decisions.rationale: The user-variable panel and normalizeWindowPosition both mutated the live config object. Building fresh objects keeps persistence correct even if the patch rule is tightened later, and removes the hidden dependency on it.

rejected_alternatives.option: Rely on the new patch rule alone
rejected_alternatives.reason: It leaves both writers one refactor away from silently losing data again, with no test pinning the shape.

decisions.title: Reject prototype-reserved keys for plugin platform and user-variable keys on both sides
decisions.rationale: These strings are used as plain-object property names in pluginMeta, and the utility host runs plugin code so it is compromisable; main must re-validate rather than trust the host's check.

rejected_alternatives.option: Guard only the immer writers with Object.hasOwn
rejected_alternatives.reason: It patches the symptom at one call site and leaves every future pluginMeta writer exposed.

decisions.title: Measure Map/Set/Error contents in the IPC payload estimator and validate pluginMeta nesting
decisions.rationale: Structured clone transports Map/Set, but their contents live in internal slots so Object.entries sized them at ~0 bytes and let oversized payloads past the 512KB cap. pluginMeta entries were also unconstrained below the top level.

rejected_alternatives.option: Throw on any non-plain object in the estimator
rejected_alternatives.reason: Other channels legitimately pass Date and typed arrays; counting each type keeps the cap meaningful without narrowing the transport.

decisions.title: Ship the persistence fix and the review findings as one commit
decisions.rationale: The updated app-config regression test asserts on both the panel/window writers and the new pluginMeta validation, so splitting would leave an intermediate tree whose tests fail.

rejected_alternatives.option: Split into a persistence commit and a hardening commit
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would require rewriting the shared test file per commit and break bisectability.

bugs.symptom: Plugin user variables were never stored: the app could not see the values and every restart lost the input, while variables saved by older versions still loaded normally.
bugs.root_cause: The panel mutated the object returned by AppConfig.getConfig("private.pluginMeta") and passed the same reference to setConfig; createChangedConfigPatch compared with Object.is, produced an empty patch, and never sent the IPC to main.
bugs.fix: Build a fresh meta object in the panel, keep object-typed values in the patch, and surface a failure toast instead of reporting success.
bugs.lesson: getConfig hands out the live config object; a writer that mutates it destroys the very change detection it depends on.

bugs.symptom: Off-screen lyric and minimode windows were moved back on screen but the corrected position was never persisted.
bugs.root_cause: normalizeWindowPosition mutated the caller's position object, which is the live config value, then wrote back the same reference.
bugs.fix: Normalize into a copy and persist that copy.
bugs.lesson: The same mutate-then-write shape existed twice; the test now pins both.

bugs.symptom: A plugin declaring platform or a user-variable key named "__proto__" could write onto Object.prototype in the main renderer through the immer pluginMeta writers, silently disabling every plugin.
bugs.root_cause: platform and variable keys were only type/length checked, yet are used directly as plain-object property names.
bugs.fix: Reject __proto__/constructor/prototype in the utility host and re-validate in main; skip no-op drag writes.
bugs.lesson: Plugin-supplied metadata reaching a privileged renderer must be key-sanitized, not just size-bounded.

bugs.symptom: A compromised renderer could push multi-megabyte Map/Set payloads past the 512KB app-config cap into main-process memory.
bugs.root_cause: estimatePayloadBytes sized objects via Object.entries, which returns an empty list for Map/Set whose contents live in internal slots.
bugs.fix: Count Map/Set/Error contents explicitly and validate pluginMeta entry counts, types, and string lengths at the IPC boundary.
bugs.lesson: A byte estimator must cover every type the transport can carry, or the cap is decorative.

summary: fix(playback): stop skip loop when the output device disappears

decisions.title: Classify a dead output endpoint as its own error kind in the libmpv host
decisions.rationale: libmpv ends the file with MPV_END_FILE_REASON_ERROR whether the media is broken or the audio device vanished, and the renderer only has that one signal. Tagging the snapshot with errorKind lets TrackPlayer keep the media-failure policy (skip) away from a device problem that every following track would hit too.

rejected_alternatives.option: Match the mpv log text emitted by the ao module
rejected_alternatives.reason: Log strings are not part of the client API and drift between mpv builds; the end-file error code plus an audio-device-list membership check is stable.

rejected_alternatives.option: Trust MPV_ERROR_AO_INIT_FAILED alone
rejected_alternatives.reason: It does not cover a device that disappears while the file is already loaded on some backends, so the selected id is also checked against the live device list.

decisions.title: Poll audio-device-list in the host instead of listening to Chromium devicechange
decisions.rationale: The main renderer never gets media permission (setPermissionCheckHandler returns false), so Chromium exposes one placeholder device per kind and hides hotplug detail. libmpv already owns the authoritative list, and re-reading it measured 0.014ms per call, so a 1Hz probe while a source is loaded is cheaper than the broken browser path.

rejected_alternatives.option: Grant the renderer media-device permission so enumerateDevices reports real devices
rejected_alternatives.reason: It widens the permission surface of a window that runs third-party plugin UI, for data the audio backend already has.

rejected_alternatives.option: Probe unconditionally on a timer
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would keep mpv's hotplug monitor alive while idle for no benefit; the preference only matters while something is playing.

decisions.title: Fall back to the default output and reload the track rather than only pausing
decisions.rationale: The error already made libmpv unload the file, so pausing alone leaves the play button dead and the next track fails on the same missing device. Falling back to auto and re-opening at the last position makes both preference values work: continue playing on the new device, or sit paused but resumable.

rejected_alternatives.option: Only pause and leave the device selection untouched
rejected_alternatives.reason: Every subsequent play attempt still targets the removed endpoint, which is the loop this commit removes.

rejected_alternatives.option: Overwrite playMusic.audioOutputDevice with auto
rejected_alternatives.reason: It silently discards the user's choice; the fallback is runtime-only and the preferred device is re-applied when it reappears.

decisions.title: Deduplicate the device-loss policy but never the recovery
decisions.rationale: One unplug produces both an error snapshot and a device-removed flag, in either order. A single guard would let whichever arrived first swallow the reload. The policy path is time-windowed while the reload path has its own throttle, which also caps recovery at one attempt when the fallback device fails too.

rejected_alternatives.option: Suppress the removed flag whenever the same snapshot is an error
rejected_alternatives.reason: It only covers the simultaneous case; when the probe fires first the reload would still be dropped.

bugs.symptom: With a specific output device selected, unplugging it made the player skip through the whole queue instead of stopping, even with "pause when the audio device is removed" chosen.
bugs.root_cause: libmpv ended the file with an AO error; the host reported it as a generic playback error, the controller mapped it to ErrorReason.EmptyResource, and TrackPlayer applied playMusic.playError (default skip). Each following track failed on the same missing device, so the skip repeated.
bugs.fix: The host tags AO failures as errorKind "audio-device", the controller raises ErrorReason.AudioDeviceUnavailable, and TrackPlayer handles it before emitting PlayerEvents.Error so the skip policy is never reached.
bugs.lesson: An error that will recur identically on every queue item must not be routed through a per-track retry policy.

bugs.symptom: The "pause when the audio device is removed" preference had no effect at all.
bugs.root_cause: bootstrap compared navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices() lengths, but the session denies media permission, so Chromium returns one blank placeholder per kind and the count is constant.
bugs.fix: Removed the browser-based detection; the libmpv host reports output-device add/remove from audio-device-list and TrackPlayer applies the preference.
bugs.lesson: Chromium device enumeration is permission-gated; a count comparison silently degrades to a no-op instead of failing.

bugs.symptom: Switching the output device back to Default left playback on the previously selected device after the next track loaded.
bugs.root_cause: activateNative only sent the output-device command when sinkId was non-empty, so an empty (auto) id never reached libmpv and audio-device kept its old value.
bugs.fix: Always send output-device on load; an empty id maps to auto in the host.
bugs.lesson: A falsy value that means "reset to default" cannot be used as the guard for whether to send the command.

tests.notes: mpv v0.41.0 returns wasapi/{guid} ids matching the stored preference; 0.014ms per re-read.

summary: feat(discovery): rebuild recommend and toplist pages around an editorial layout

decisions.title: Replace the pill source tabs with an underline rail driven by a measured sliding indicator
decisions.rationale: The shared tab-list-container chrome (rounded container, filled selected pill, colored glow) competes with the new page headline and reads as a toy control next to hairline rules and a 2.8rem title. An underline rail carries the selection with only text weight plus a 2px accent bar, so the header keeps a single focal point. The bar is positioned from offsetLeft/offsetWidth of the active tab rather than per-tab pseudo-elements because a single travelling element makes the switch legible as motion between two sources instead of one underline vanishing and another appearing.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep the existing .tab-list-container styling used by search and theme views
rejected_alternatives.reason: Those pages have no display headline, so the segmented block is the primary control there. On the discovery pages it lands directly under an h1 and an eyebrow and duplicates their visual weight.

rejected_alternatives.option: Render the underline as a per-tab ::after that scales from 0 to 1 on selection
rejected_alternatives.reason: It needs no measurement, but every switch cross-fades two separate bars instead of moving one, which loses the spatial relationship between adjacent sources.

rejected_alternatives.option: Track the active tab with a MutationObserver on the headlessui state attribute
rejected_alternatives.reason: Tab.List already exposes selectedIndex through its render prop, so observing DOM attributes would add a second source of truth for state the library hands over directly.

decisions.title: Pass the Tab.List node through state rather than a shared ref object
decisions.rationale: Measurement lives in a child of Tab.List so it can consume the selectedIndex render prop. React commits effects bottom-up, so the child's useLayoutEffect runs before the parent host element's ref is attached, leaving railRef.current null on the first pass: the indicator would stay unmounted and the ResizeObserver would never attach until an unrelated re-render. A callback ref that sets state re-renders the child once the node exists, which makes the first measured frame deterministic.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep useRef and read railRef.current inside the child effects
rejected_alternatives.reason: It type-checks and lints clean but silently skips the first measurement, so the indicator only appears after some later render happens to run the effect again.

rejected_alternatives.option: Hoist measurement into the parent and pass selectedIndex down from Tab.Group
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would push tab-strip layout state into both page components and duplicate the wiring across the recommend and toplist views.

decisions.title: Make the flat editorial chip the base style for the tag row and let glass only remap borders
decisions.rationale: The tag filters previously stacked pill radius, backdrop blur, inset shadow and a hover lift, and the glass selected state used a 14% warm tint over a translucent surface that is nearly indistinguishable from an idle chip. Base styles now carry one crisp chip spec with an ink-fill selected state built from --appTextPrimary over --backgroundColor, so contrast holds in every theme; the ui-style blocks only adjust border tokens.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep the warm tint and raise its mix percentage
rejected_alternatives.reason: It stays a tint over a translucent surface, so the selected chip still competes with hover rather than reading as a committed state.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep the flat block's hardcoded #111214 fill and #fff text
rejected_alternatives.reason: Those values assume a light canvas; on dark themes the chip collapses into the background. Theme tokens invert correctly on their own.

decisions.title: Inset the toplist row dividers and drop the list's top border
decisions.rationale: A top border on the container plus a bottom border on every row closed the ranked list into a boxed table and drew a rule under the last item, which sat oddly beside the featured cover card. Dividers now render as a ::before inset to the artwork column, skip the last row, and fade on the hovered row and the one above it so the highlight block stays unbroken under glass's rounded row radius.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep full-bleed borders and only remove the last-child rule
rejected_alternatives.reason: The divider would still cut across the rounded hover surface in glass mode, where rows carry --listRowRadius.

rejected_alternatives.option: Drop dividers entirely and separate rows with spacing
rejected_alternatives.reason: Rank, artwork, title and meta form a dense four-column row; without a rule the columns stop reading as discrete entries.

decisions.title: Reserve the selected tab's bold metrics with a hidden ghost copy
decisions.rationale: The active source switches to weight 800, which widens the label and would shift every following tab plus the measured indicator on each selection. A visually hidden zero-height ::after carrying the same text at the bold weight pins each tab to its widest state, so the rail never reflows.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep one weight and signal selection through colour alone
rejected_alternatives.reason: Tertiary-to-primary colour alone is a weak cue at 0.92rem when the rail sits on a busy header.

rejected_alternatives.option: Give each tab a fixed min-width
rejected_alternatives.reason: Source names range from short latin labels to longer CJK platform names, so any single width either clips or leaves large gaps.

decisions.title: Surface the active tag inside the expanded tag panel
decisions.rationale: The trigger button showed the current filter but the panel rendered every tag identically, so opening it gave no indication of what was already applied. TagPanel now receives selectedId and reuses the same ink-fill highlight as the row chips.

rejected_alternatives.option: Leave the panel unmarked because the trigger already shows the value
rejected_alternatives.reason: The trigger is covered by the panel while it is open, which is exactly when the user is comparing options.

bugs.symptom: Selected-state styling on the source tabs would silently drop while the pointer was over the active tab.
bugs.root_cause: The stylesheet matched [data-headlessui-state="selected"] exactly, but headlessui joins active slot flags into one space-separated value, so the attribute becomes "selected hover" on hover and the exact-match selector stops applying.
bugs.fix: The rebuilt component targets the discrete [data-selected] attribute that headlessui emits alongside the combined value, which is unaffected by additional concurrent states.
bugs.lesson: data-headlessui-state is a value list; style against the per-state data-* attributes rather than matching the joined string.

bugs.symptom: history.state.usr threw when the discovery pages were opened on a fresh navigation entry.
bugs.root_cause: Three call sites read history.state.usr without guarding history.state, which is null until the router writes a state object.

decisions.title: Randomize the initial recommend-sheet tag per plugin
decisions.rationale: The recommend-sheet body previously bootstrapped from history state or the default tag, so a fresh visit repeatedly landed on the same category. The new helper builds a de-duplicated candidate list from pinned and grouped tags and samples one when tag data is ready.
tradeoffs: The first visible category is less predictable, but the page surfaces more of each plugin's recommendation taxonomy.
assumptions: Tag ids are stable enough to de-duplicate candidates and remember the last random choice per plugin.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep restoring history.state.usr.tag as the initial selection
rejected_alternatives.reason: It preserves navigation state but prevents the requested fresh random entry behavior from taking effect on repeat visits.

rejected_alternatives.option: Sample only grouped tags and ignore pinned tags
rejected_alternatives.reason: Pinned tags are part of the plugin-provided recommendation surface and should participate in the same initial choice pool.

side_effects: When a plugin exposes more than one tag, the next random entry avoids immediately repeating the previous tag for that plugin.

decisions.title: Keep the expanded-panel seed tag aligned with the selected tag
decisions.rationale: The same random tag now initializes both firstTag and selectedTag, so opening the tag panel starts from the exact category currently rendered in the sheet list.
tradeoffs: The prior cached-tag branch is removed, so route history no longer overrides the initial random choice.
assumptions: The active plugin hash is the correct boundary for remembering the previous random selection.

rejected_alternatives.option: Set only selectedTag and leave firstTag unchanged
rejected_alternatives.reason: That can make the collapsed trigger and expanded panel disagree on which tag seeded the current view.

summary: fix(recommend): keep random tag stable on return

decisions.title: Cache recommendation tags per plugin for the renderer session
decisions.rationale: The route entry is destroyed when opening a remote sheet and returning, so using history.state to remember the random tag still allowed a fresh random pick. A module-level per-plugin cache survives page unmounts within the running renderer and only initializes each plugin once.
tradeoffs: The random seed is scoped to the current app run instead of every visit, which favors navigation stability over frequent variety.
assumptions: Plugin hashes remain stable while the renderer session is alive.

rejected_alternatives.option: Persist the random tag in route state
rejected_alternatives.reason: Opening a sheet via navigate creates a different route entry, so returning can remount without the expected state and repeat the randomization.

rejected_alternatives.option: Persist the random tag in AppConfig
rejected_alternatives.reason: The requested behavior is session-scoped startup randomness, not a cross-restart user preference.

side_effects: Manual tag selections update the same session cache, so returning from a sheet preserves the user's current filter.

bugs.symptom: After opening a recommended sheet and returning, the recommend page picked a different random tag and refreshed the list.
bugs.root_cause: Randomization ran whenever tag data arrived and no reliable restored tag was available; route state was not stable across the detail-page navigation flow.
bugs.fix: Store firstTag and selectedTag in a module-level map keyed by plugin hash, restore from it before randomizing, and refresh the cache when the user changes tags.
bugs.lesson: A UI state that must survive route unmount/remount should live outside the route entry when the navigation flow does not preserve that entry state.

decisions.title: Make the rendered music list own scrolling in nested local-music views
decisions.rationale: Album, artist, and folder pages all render MusicList inside a right-hand detail column. Assigning overflow to the list container keeps the virtualizer, scroll padding, and the visibly moving element aligned, while min-height: 0 and hidden overflow on the flex wrappers prevent an outer competing scrollbar.
tradeoffs: The right-hand wrapper no longer acts as a generic scroll surface; future content added beside MusicList must declare its own scrolling behavior.
assumptions: Each nested right-hand column continues to contain a direct .music-list-container child.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep .right-part as the scroll element and only adjust bottom padding
rejected_alternatives.reason: The virtualizer and music-bar clearance would remain coupled to a wrapper instead of the list component that owns the rows.

side_effects: Glass-mode music-bar clearance is applied to the local view containers, and embedded base lists are prevented from shrinking.

decisions.title: Preserve the intended local list action shape in flat mode
decisions.rationale: The local list action is not part of the compact icon-only action group, so excluding it from the global circular-radius selector lets its component styling determine the appropriate shape.
assumptions: The list-view action component supplies its own border radius.

rejected_alternatives.option: Keep forcing every local list action to a circle
rejected_alternatives.reason: That global override conflates the wider list action with icon-only controls.

bugs.symptom: Nested album, artist, and folder lists could use a different scroll surface from their virtualized row container, and bottom rows could collide with the glass music bar.
bugs.root_cause: The right-hand wrapper owned overflow while virtualization and music-bar spacing were split across wrapper and list-level selectors.
bugs.fix: Move overflow to the direct music-list container, point getScrollElement at that node, constrain the flex wrappers, and apply music-bar clearance at the local-view container level.
bugs.lesson: A virtualized list, its visible scrollbar, and its fixed-overlay clearance should target the same scrolling element.

summary: feat(video): add production MV playback and downloads

decisions.title: Model video playback separately from audio quality
decisions.rationale: Plugins now expose getMvSource and verified video-quality metadata without coercing resolution labels into audio-quality keys.
tradeoffs: The plugin and IPC contracts gain a dedicated video path.
assumptions: Plugins return structured-cloneable source metadata.
side_effects: Existing media-source quality handling now accepts plugin-reported string qualities.

decisions.title: Proxy remote video sources through a validated local session
decisions.rationale: The main process validates upstream URLs and headers, rewrites HLS playlists, preserves range requests, and exposes narrow renderer/preload APIs for playback, size probing, and downloads.
tradeoffs: Playback creates short-lived proxy sessions that require explicit cleanup.
assumptions: The main window is the only renderer allowed to register video sessions.
side_effects: Remote artwork requests use no-referrer normalization for compatible providers.

decisions.title: Only present verified qualities and start at the highest real option
decisions.rationale: Declared plugin qualities are treated as probe candidates, then de-duplicated by actual quality and source fingerprint before display. The player requests the highest candidate first and falls back downward.
tradeoffs: Opening a video performs bounded parallel metadata probes.
assumptions: Source URL fingerprints and plugin-reported qualities identify fallback duplicates.
side_effects: Quality labels are normalized to uppercase and file sizes are shown in compact aligned menus.

decisions.title: Use independent sessions for quality-selectable downloads
decisions.rationale: The download button opens the same verified quality list and registers a dedicated proxy session, so playback quality changes do not interrupt an active download.
tradeoffs: A download briefly owns a second proxy session.
assumptions: The existing node runtime download pipeline remains the durable file writer.
side_effects: MV entry badges appear in lists, queue, music bar, and context menus.

bugs.symptom: Several requested quality labels could point to the same video and show duplicate file sizes, while a 4K video opened at 1080P.
bugs.root_cause: The UI treated declared request keys as verified qualities and initialized playback at a fixed 1080P key.
bugs.fix: Probe each candidate, de-duplicate actual sources, and select the highest verified quality by default.
bugs.lesson: Capability declarations are candidates; user-facing quality lists must be built from resolved source evidence.
